messages:
Maria: Heads up — spotted inconsistent phrasing in the SOC2 audit export doc and a broken link to the export SDK example. Can we triage?

Aj Patel: Thanks — which page? pinging @Kevin and @Sylvia

Maria: docs/security/audit-export.md around line ~120: uses 'tenant data' vs 'tenant-scoped data'. Also link points to /sdk/python/export -> 404. :grimacing:

Kevin Liu: Good catch. I'll check the SDK repo — looks like examples moved in v2. Should we include both curl and python snippets?

Sylvia Gomez: Yes. Also for SOC2 wording we need to avoid 'we store' phrasing. Compliance asked for 'retained by default for 90 days' + a link to the retention policy. Legal specifically: 'avoid implying indefinite retention'.

Aj Patel: I can open a small PR. I'll handle the snippet updates if Maria wants to do the language edits. Proposed python snippet:

```python
from redwood import AuditExportClient
client = AuditExportClient(api_key="<REDACTED>")
client.export(scope='tenant', format='jsonl')
```

Maria: Nice. Add `region='us-east-1'` in the constructor for the example. Also update the doc link to the new SDK path: https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk/python/v2/audit_export

Kevin Liu: Opening PR now — #4523. Changes: fix phrasing, update link, add curl + python snippets, and add sample-output unit test. Assigning @Sylvia for compliance review.

Sylvia Gomez: On it. Quick note — SOC2 phrasing: replace 'we may retain' with 'retention period is 90 days by default' and add a short sentence about exceptions (legal hold). I'll leave inline comments on the PR.

compliance-bot: Automated check: PR title doesn't include 'soc2' — suggestion: 'docs: soc2 audit export phrasing & sdk snippet fix'

Maria: :thumbsup: Added to CHANGELOG.md. Thanks everyone — target merge EOD.
